query: For a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain the accelerated coupled degradation and why it occurs? Specify a controlled comparison capable of distinguishing the proposed explanation, predict the changes in total degradation and the individual wear and corrosion responses relative to a matched baseline, define the relevant boundary conditions, identify supporting evidence, and give a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In a multiphase eutectic high-entropy alloy at elevated temperature, accelerated coupled degradation under simultaneous wear and corrosion is governed by tribo-galvanic selective dissolution localized at interphase (lamellar) boundaries. Repeated oxide-film rupture during sliding exposes dissimilar phases with a nobility mismatch; the more anodic lamellae dissolve to form interfacial trenches that mechanically undercut the harder/cathodic lamellae, promoting micro-chipping and delamination. This feedback between galvanic boundary dissolution and mechanically assisted removal produces a total material loss greater than the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with fine lamellar or interpenetrating phases (e.g., ordered B2-like and FCC-like constituents) exhibiting hardness/nobility contrast, high interphase boundary density, slight compositional segregation, and a thin native oxide.
generation.intervention: Expose the alloy to simultaneous sliding wear and electrochemically active corrosive environment at elevated temperature (tribocorrosion), compared to matched single-mode baselines (wear-only in inert medium; corrosion-only without sliding) and to controls that suppress galvanic dissolution (cathodic polarization) or remove micro-galvanic couples (single-phase homogenized variant).
generation.conditions: Electrolyte: 3.5 wt% NaCl(aq), air-saturated, 80 ± 5 °C. Tribology: reciprocating alumina counterbody (6 mm ball), 5 N normal load, 5 mm stroke, 2 Hz, 60 min, ambient pressure. Electrochemistry: open-circuit potential (OCP) during tribocorrosion; potentiostatic cathodic polarization at −0.2 V vs OCP for suppression test. Baselines: wear-only in deoxygenated inert oil at 80 °C with identical sliding; corrosion-only as static immersion at 80 °C for 60 min without sliding.
generation.structural_mediator: Nobility contrast between eutectic lamellae (micro-galvanic coupling), high density of interphase boundaries, and a thermally grown tribo-oxide that is cyclically ruptured and locally porous, allowing electrolyte ingress along phase boundaries.
generation.mechanism:
- Elevated temperature accelerates oxide growth on each phase, but sliding continuously ruptures/abrades the tribo-oxide, exposing fresh, compositionally dissimilar lamellae.
- In the electrolyte, the nobler phase acts as a local cathode and the less noble phase as an anode; galvanic current concentrates along interphase boundaries and at freshly ruptured spots.
- Selective anodic dissolution along boundaries produces trenching/undercutting beneath harder lamellae; porous/cracked tribo-oxide facilitates electrolyte penetration and repassivation-rupture cycling.
- Undercutting concentrates contact stresses, causing micro-chipping and delamination of the harder lamellae; the resulting debris further abrades the surface and removes nascent films.
- Fresh metal exposure sustains high transient anodic currents and prevents stable passivation, creating a positive feedback that yields total material loss exceeding the additive sum of wear-only and corrosion-only.
generation.predicted_outcome:
- Relative to the matched baseline sum (wear-only + corrosion-only at 80 °C), the total material loss rate under simultaneous wear+corrosion (tribocorrosion at OCP) increases (positive synergy). Expected synergy factor S = K_tc/(K_w + K_c) in the range ~1.5–3 (direction confident; magnitude uncertain), where K denotes material loss per sliding distance or per time.
- The average corrosion rate during sliding (from time-averaged current) increases versus static corrosion at 80 °C, with current spikes synchronized to sliding passes; a 2–5× increase is plausible (magnitude uncertain).
- The mechanical wear component (inferred by subtracting electrochemical mass loss) increases relative to wear-only due to interfacial undermining and micro-delamination.
- Wear-track cross-sections show interphase trenching (sub-micron to a few microns deep) and lamellar pull-out; debris enriched in the nominally cathodic/harder phase appears.
- Under cathodic polarization (−0.2 V vs OCP), synergy collapses toward additivity (S ≲ 1.2), interfacial trenching is strongly suppressed, and current spikes diminish.
- A single-phase, compositionally homogenized control of similar bulk hardness exhibits near-additive behavior (S ~ 1.0–1.2) and lacks boundary-localized attack under the same tribocorrosion conditions.
generation.baseline: Additive expectation: K_base = K_w (wear-only in inert medium at 80 °C with identical sliding) + K_c (static corrosion-only at 80 °C for the same duration). Predictions are expressed relative to K_base and to the individual baselines K_w and K_c.
generation.boundary:
- Applies to multiphase eutectic microstructures with fine lamellar spacing (≲ a few micrometers) and a measurable nobility mismatch between phases (≫ ~50 mV) in the given electrolyte at elevated temperature, and to sliding conditions that repeatedly rupture the tribo-oxide.
- Diminished or no effect when: (i) the alloy is single-phase or lamellae are coarse/sparsely intersecting the surface; (ii) the environment is non-conductive or dry (no ionic conduction, galvanic currents negligible); (iii) a stable, adherent tribo-oxide glaze forms that is not ruptured under the applied contact; or (iv) temperatures/loadings outside the stated range either prevent passivation entirely or induce gross softening/melting that changes the wear regime.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitudes (e.g., exact synergy factor, current amplification, trench depth) depend on the specific phase chemistries, lamellar spacing, oxide adherence, and exact electrochemical kinetics; only the directions and qualitative ordering are predicted with high confidence. If the tribo-oxide becomes uniformly protective at 80 °C in the chosen electrolyte, the synergy may be smaller than anticipated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three specimens: (A) as-cast eutectic HEA with lamellar microstructure; (B) homogenized single-phase variant of similar bulk hardness; (C) specimen A tested under cathodic polarization. For each, measure (i) wear-only in inert oil at 80 °C; (ii) corrosion-only static immersion at 80 °C; (iii) tribocorrosion at OCP in 3.5 wt% NaCl at 80 °C under the defined sliding; and (iv) for C, tribocorrosion at −0.2 V vs OCP. Record in situ electrochemical current during sliding, friction, and measure material loss by 3D profilometry. Perform SEM/FIB cross-sections and EDS maps of wear tracks to detect boundary-localized attack and delamination.
measurements: Total material loss per unit sliding distance (profilometry-derived wear volume)
Electrochemical current-time during sliding (to compute corrosion charge)
Open-circuit potential and potentiostatic control logs
SEM/FIB cross-sections of wear tracks with EDS phase mapping
Quantification of interfacial trench density and depth
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if any of the following are observed: (1) Specimen A exhibits near-additive behavior (S ≤ 1.2) at OCP while microscopy shows no preferential boundary trenching or lamellae delamination; (2) Applying cathodic polarization to specimen A does not reduce synergy (S remains > 1.5) and boundary trenching persists; (3) The single-phase control B shows synergy comparable to A (S within ±10% of A) and similar boundary-localized features under identical conditions; or (4) Sliding does not produce increased corrosion currents versus static (no current spikes and no increase in average current).
